behaviours.name: node label domain
behaviours.statement: A public query may name only these node labels.

behaviours.name: relationship domain
behaviours.statement: A public query may name only these relationship types.

behaviours.name: endpoint pairs
behaviours.statement: A relationship type is only meaningful on its declared endpoint pairs; the matrix records every pair rather than the type alone.

behaviours.name: root operations
behaviours.statement: The first token of a raw query must be one of these.

behaviours.name: clause vocabulary is published but not enforced
behaviours.statement: CYPHER_SUPPORTED_CLAUSES is published in the contract document and bound to CYPHER_WHITELIST, but validate_cypher_read_only consults only the blacklist and the root operation. A clause outside this list is admitted unless it is the root token or a blacklisted word.

behaviours.name: related-context directions
behaviours.statement: Traversal direction is a closed public domain.

behaviours.name: related-context depths
behaviours.statement: Public traversal depth is 1 or 2, not an open range.

behaviours.name: graph layers
behaviours.statement: The layer selector is a closed domain.

behaviours.name: similarity range
behaviours.statement: Similarity is a unit interval; the minimum is part of the contract.

behaviours.name: timestamp normalization at the typed boundary
behaviours.statement: TIMESTAMP columns remain typed inside the graph and are converted to ISO text only when KGService constructs its public result.

behaviours.name: vector search stays on the structured graph-store port
behaviours.statement: Pulse similarity retrieval calls graph_store.vector_search; it does not depend on a backend-specific raw Cypher vector function.

behaviours.name: default row cap
behaviours.statement: A caller that passes no max_rows gets this many rows.

behaviours.name: maximum row cap
behaviours.statement: A caller cannot ask for more rows than this.

behaviours.name: default timeout
behaviours.statement: A caller that passes no timeout gets this budget in milliseconds.

behaviours.name: maximum timeout
behaviours.statement: A caller cannot ask for a longer budget than this.

behaviours.name: traversal depth cap
behaviours.statement: The depth an UNBOUNDED variable-length path is bounded to. An EXPLICIT upper bound is left alone: _bound_relationship_segment returns the segment unchanged once it finds digits after '..', so '*1..21' is not clamped to 20.

behaviours.name: LIMIT injection
behaviours.statement: A query with no LIMIT outside comments and string literals has 'LIMIT <max_rows>' appended after a trailing semicolon is stripped.

behaviours.name: path bounding runs before the layer rewrite
behaviours.statement: Bounding happens first, so the layer rewrite sees the bounded text and still refuses it: its guard matches any '*' inside relationship brackets.

behaviours.name: comments stripped before tokenizing
behaviours.statement: A keyword hidden in a // or /* */ comment is not a token.

behaviours.name: NFKC normalization
behaviours.statement: Homoglyphs are folded before the blacklist is applied, so a fullwidth DELETE is one.

behaviours.name: string literals blanked
behaviours.statement: A blacklisted word inside a quoted literal is data, not a token.

behaviours.name: write attempt
behaviours.statement: A blacklisted token anywhere in the query is a security refusal.

behaviours.name: unsupported root
behaviours.statement: A non-mutating root operation outside the subset is a DIFFERENT refusal, so a client can correct the query without it being treated as an attempted write.

behaviours.name: unenforceable canonical filter
behaviours.statement: Anonymous nodes and variable-length traversal cannot be filtered safely, so the contract refuses rather than risk leaking working-layer rows.

behaviours.name: missing executor
behaviours.statement: A missing cypher_executor is a composition error, not an empty result.

behaviours.name: canonical predicate injected per named variable
behaviours.statement: Each named node variable in a MATCH pattern gains its own layer predicate.

behaviours.name: existing WHERE is parenthesised
behaviours.statement: The caller's own WHERE is wrapped in parentheses, so an OR in it cannot widen past the injected layer predicate.

behaviours.name: include_working skips the rewrite
behaviours.statement: The rewrite is applied only when include_working is false.

behaviours.name: paired execution
behaviours.statement: The paired call is used only when the layer rewrite actually fired and the executor exposes it; otherwise a single execute_read_only runs.

behaviours.name: projection applied to every result
behaviours.statement: Both the paired and the single path return through the same projection, which carries the filter mode and the comparison result into the envelope.

behaviours.name: columns
behaviours.statement: The projection reads the backend column vector used to interpret positional rows.

behaviours.name: row count
behaviours.statement: The returned envelope recomputes row_count after canonical projection.

behaviours.name: truncation
behaviours.statement: The backend truncation flag is preserved and contributes to whether an omitted-row count is exact.

behaviours.name: omitted row count
behaviours.statement: The envelope reports omitted working rows together with exactness, source and returned-window scope fields.

behaviours.name: omitted row count exactness
behaviours.statement: Consumers can distinguish an exact count from a non-observable one.

behaviours.name: omitted layer counts
behaviours.statement: Paired execution can expose the omitted rows grouped by graph layer.
